verses.text: Solomon son of David took firm control of his kingdom. The LORD his God was with him and made him very great.
Solomon spoke to all Israel: to the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, to the judges, and to all the leaders in Israel, the heads of families.
Then Solomon and the whole assembly with him went to the high place at Gibeon, because God's Tent of Meeting was there. It was the tent that Moses, the LORD's servant, had made in the desert.
David had already brought God's ark up from Kiriath Jearim to the place he had prepared for it. He had set up a tent for it in Jerusalem.
But the bronze altar that Bezalel son of Uri, the son of Hur, had made was there in Gibeon, in front of the LORD's tabernacle. So Solomon and the assembly went there to ask the LORD for guidance.
Solomon went up to the bronze altar before the LORD at the Tent of Meeting, and he offered a thousand burnt offerings on it.
That night God appeared to Solomon and said to him, "Ask for whatever you want me to give you."
Solomon answered God, "You showed great and faithful love to my father David, and you have made me king in his place.
Now, LORD God, let your promise to my father David come true, because you have made me king over a people as many as the dust of the earth.
Give me wisdom and knowledge, so I can lead these people. Who could ever rule this great people of yours?"

God said to Solomon, "This is what is in your heart. You did not ask for riches, wealth, or honour, or for the death of your enemies, or even for a long life. Instead, you asked for wisdom and knowledge so you can rule my people, over whom I have made you king.
So I will give you wisdom and knowledge. I will also give you riches, wealth, and honour, more than any king before you ever had, or any king after you will have."
Then Solomon left the high place at Gibeon, in front of the Tent of Meeting, and went back to Jerusalem. And he ruled over Israel.
Solomon gathered chariots and horses. He had one thousand four hundred chariots and twelve thousand horses. He kept some in the chariot cities and some with him in Jerusalem.
The king made silver and gold as common in Jerusalem as stones, and cedar wood as common as the fig trees in the western foothills.
Solomon's horses were brought from Egypt and from Kue. The king's traders bought them in Kue.
They brought chariots from Egypt for six hundred pieces of silver each, and horses for one hundred and fifty each. They also sold them to all the kings of the Hittites and the kings of Syria.
